claim: The paired delay this experiment was designed to test could not be computed. The N=64 per-seed trajectories for seeds 56, 57, 58, 62 and 63 were not in the provided results, and the lab files could not be opened. All 5 N=256 runs completed and meet the side conditions: final accel_step margin is 0.118 to 0.187 at layer 4 (R2 0.85 to 0.90, controls 0.67 to 0.78, so >= 0.1 in every seed), and val_mse_ratio ends at 11.3 to 13.3 (above 1). From the 5-step trajectories, the half-final step (seeds 56/57/58/62/63) is 85/75/100/90/95, a range of 25 steps, and the persistent 0.1-bar step is 95/155/115/95/100, a range of 60 steps. Only two N=64 values can be paired, both quoted in an open question: seed 56 at step 80 and seed 62 at step 100. That gives 0.1-bar delays of +15 and -5. Force has no lasting signal: an early transient margin of 0.16 to 0.21 at steps 10-15 falls to about 0 to 0.02 by steps 105-120, compared with accel_step's 0.12 to 0.19.
confidence_note: The primary criterion, a half-final delay of at least +15 in 4 of 5 seeds with a mean of at least +20, needs the per-seed N=64 half-final steps, and they were not available to this analysis. The verdict is inconclusive because data was missing, not because the effect is absent. Joining the N=64 arm trajectories from the 5-step N=64 runs of these seeds and recomputing the delays would decide supported or refuted. Three caveats from the N=256 arm itself. (1) The two pairable 0.1-bar delays (+15, -5) are smaller than the earlier 10-step comparison for seeds 56-58 (+20/+70/+30), so some of the earlier delay may have come from mixed checkpoint spacing. (2) The half-final measure is tighter than the 0.1 bar within N=256 (25 vs 60 steps), but it is confounded with plateau height. Seed 57 has the lowest final margin (0.118, control 0.778) and so the earliest half-final step (75), yet the latest 0.1-bar step (155). It dwells at 0.093-0.099 from step 125 to 150. (3) For seed 62, probes_final.formed_at_step = 100, but the trajectory first crosses persistently at 95, another case of the one-checkpoint lag. All 5 runs completed 300/300 steps with 5 controls each.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261012-070236-2512 (issue 1): Accepted. The N=64 arm (exp-20261012-063043-b06b) completed in the same cycle. The finding's 'data missing' explanation was the same-batch join failure, which the experiment note now records as fixed. Joined per seed (56/57/58/62/63): half-final delays are +15/+10/+30/+30/+10, so 3 of 5 seeds are >= +15 and the mean is +19. expected_if_true (4 of 5 seeds and mean >= +20) fails, and expected_if_false fails too, with only 2 of 5 at <= +10. Persistent 0.1-bar delays are +15/+70/+25/-5/+5, spanning 75 steps against 20 for half-final. The verdict stays inconclusive, but because the criteria are borderline, not because data was missing. Across all 16 matched e<=0.5 seeds the half-final delay has never been below +10, so the direction is consistent and only the size is uncertain. I am not proposing another e<=0.5 replication. This cycle tests instead whether the delay depends on eccentricity (N=256 at e<=0.7, paired with an existing N=64 arm, with both trajectories read from run records and inconclusive declared if either is unavailable).

Response to review r-20261012-070236-2512 (issue 1): Accepted. The N=64 arm (exp-20261012-063043-b06b) was available, and the note on the experiment confirms the join failure has since been fixed in the pipeline. Joined per seed (56/57/58/62/63): N=64 half-final 70/65/70/60/85 vs N=256 85/75/100/90/95 gives delays of +15/+10/+30/+30/+10. That is 3 of 5 >= +15 with a mean of +19, so expected_if_true fails. Only 2 of 5 are <= +10, so expected_if_false also fails. 0.1-bar delays are N=64 80/85/90/100/95 vs N=256 95/155/115/95/100, giving +15/+70/+25/-5/+5. The verdict stays inconclusive, and the reason is that the criteria came out borderline, not that data was missing. Across all 16 matched e<=0.5 seeds, the half-final delay is positive in every seed (+10 to +75) but rarely clears the pre-registered per-seed bars, so the honest summary is a small, consistent delay of roughly +10 to +30 steps. I am not proposing another timing arm. Further seeds are unlikely to resolve a criterion this close to the bar, so this cycle's compute goes to the eccentricity sweep instead.
